toegepas.voor: die name van mans wat hulle meer as 150 jaar gelede gekoop het
toegepas.na: die name van die mans wat dit meer as 150 jaar gelede gekoop het
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'mans wat hulle ... gekoop het' can be read as 'men whom they bought'; 'die mans wat dit' makes the men the buyers and the scrolls the thing bought, and 'die' is needed because specific men are meant.
toegepas.fout: 'mans wat hulle ... gekoop het' can be read either way round: the men who bought the scrolls, or the men whom the scrolls (or someone) bought.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'die mans wat dit ... gekoop het' makes the men the buyers without moving the meaning, and 'dit' matches the 'daarvan' already in the sentence.

toegepas.voor: 'n towerspreuk oor die siek mens gesê
toegepas.na: 'n towerspreuk oor die siek mens opgesê
toegepas.rede_vinder: A prayer or spell is 'opgesê' (recited) in Afrikaans; 'oor iemand gesê' also reads as 'said about someone'.
toegepas.fout: 'n towerspreuk ... gesê' is a loose verb for reciting a spell, and 'oor die siek mens gesê' can also read as 'said about the sick person'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'opgesê' is the exact Afrikaans verb for reciting a prayer or spell, keeps 'oor' and every other word, and adds no fact.

vlae.teks: Die kanale dra bloed, ander soorte vloeistof en lug.
vlae.rede: This sentence sits between two belief-framed sentences ('het geglo', 'het gedink') but is itself a bare present-tense statement, so on its own it reads as a fact about the body rather than what the Egyptians believed. Fixing it (for example 'Volgens hulle dra die kanale ...') shifts the claim, so it is flagged for the writer rather than changed.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: dele van die liggaam kan raak
laat_vaar_vorige.na: dele van die liggaam kan beïnvloed
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Raak' can be read as 'touch'; 'beïnvloed' says plainly that the damage affects other parts.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'raak' in the sense of 'affect' is natural, plain Afrikaans here; 'beinvloed' is a heavier word for Grade 5 and only reads differently.
